---
title: "Political Messages in Entertainment Media"
description: "Working paper — political attitudes and the non-news media environment"
date: "2023-06-01"
categories: [media and politics]
---

::: {.justified}

Research on media and political attitudes has concentrated almost entirely on news, yet news is a small share of what Americans actually watch.
Most of the modern media environment is fiction, and its effect on political behavior remains largely unexamined.
This project asks what television fiction does to political attitudes, and proposes four lines of attack: an experiment varying how a policy issue is portrayed within a storyline, a descriptive account of how much political content fictional programming actually carries, a test of whether portrayals precede or follow shifts in public opinion, and an analysis of how ideology and geography shape what people choose to watch.
It builds on Mutz and Nir (2010), close to the discipline's only sustained treatment of the question, and extends it across multiple issues, a genuine control condition, and personality predispositions in place of induced empathy.

:::

**Status.** Working paper, 2023.
